'''Jarred Jakobi Vanderbilt''' (born April 3, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected as a [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]] in high school.<ref>{{cite web|title=2017 McDonald's All-American Game boys rosters announced|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|date=January 15, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref> Vanderbilt played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the second round of the [[2018 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
[[File:20170329 MCDAAG Jarred Vanderbilt holds the ball (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Vanderbilt at the [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Vanderbilt was born in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]]. He is the son of Gwendolyn and Robert Vanderbilt. He has two older brothers, Jamal and Robert, and three older sisters, Rean, Jenae, and Tasha. His father played basketball at Wiley College. His mother played at Xavier of Louisiana. His brother, Jamal, played at Texas-Tyler and sister, Jenae, played at UTSA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/v/vanderbilt-jarred-1.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160611100728/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/v/vanderbilt-jarred-1.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 11, 2016|title=Jarred Vanderbilt|website=www.usab.com}}</ref>

Vanderbilt attended Victory Prep Academy in [[Houston, Texas]]. As a senior, he averaged 28.5 points, 13.4 rebounds and 8.8 assists per game.{{citation needed|date=February 2023}}

Vanderbilt was considered one of the best players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jarred-Vanderbilt-29987|title=Jarred Vanderbilt, Victory Prep, Small Forward|website=247sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/190952/jarred-vanderbilt|title=Jarred Vanderbilt – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles |publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/jarred-vanderbilt-1531|title=Jarred Vanderbilt, 2017 Power forward|website=n.rivals.com|access-date=August 6, 2016|archive-date=February 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227211747/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/jarred-vanderbilt-1531|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 23, 2016, Vanderbilt committed to the Kentucky Wildcats.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story?id=18339528|title=No.22 recruit Jarred Vanderbilt commits to Kentucky|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=December 23, 2016|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 23, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Despite being highly regarded coming out of high school, two injuries marred Vanderbilt's college career and he only played 14 games for the Kentucky Wildcats. He averaged 5.9 points and 7.9 rebounds in 17.0 minutes per game. Following the season he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spectrumnews1.com/splash|title=Spectrum News|website=spectrumnews1.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Denver Nuggets (2018–2020)===
On June 21, 2018, Vanderbilt was drafted by the [[Orlando Magic]] with the 41st overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He was subsequently traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-continue-add-length-second-round|title=Magic Continue to Add Length in Second Round|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2018-draft-trade-tracker|title=2018 NBA Draft Trade Tracker|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2018}}</ref> On July 11, 2018, Vanderbilt signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-vanderbilt-071118|title=The Denver Nuggets Sign Rookie Jarred Vanderbilt|date=July 11, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 11, 2018}}</ref> Vanderbilt made his NBA debut on January 25, 2019, in a 132–95 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]], playing four minutes and scoring one point with three rebounds, an assist, and one steal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/joelrush/2019/01/27/denver-nuggets-rundown-games-40-48-offense-surges-as-will-barton-gary-harris-return-from-injury/#14c330413129|title=Denver Nuggets Rundown, Games 40–48: Offense Surges As Will Barton, Gary Harris Return From Injury|first=Joel|last=Rush|work=[[Forbes#Forbes.com|Forbes.com]]|date=January 27, 2019|access-date=January 27, 2019}}</ref> On November 20, 2019, Vanderbilt was assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=We have assigned Jarred Vanderbilt to the Rio Grande Valley Vipers of the G League.|url=https://twitter.com/nuggets/status/1197259570541760512|website=Denver Nuggets on Twitter|access-date=November 22, 2019|date=November 20, 2019}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–2022)===
On February 5, 2020, Vanderbilt was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Brooklyn Nets' 2020 First Round Pick from Atlanta Hawks, Malik Beasley, Juancho Hernangomez and Jarred Vanderbilt from Denver Nuggets in 12-Player, Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-brooklyn-nets-2020-first-round-pick-atlanta-hawks-malik-beasley |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 6, 2020 |date=February 5, 2020}}</ref> Vanderbilt made his 2020 debut on December 27, 2020, in a 127–91 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], playing 15 minutes and scoring two points, seven rebounds, six assists, three steals, and a block. On January 23, 2021, Vanderbilt scored a career-high 16 points along with 11 rebounds in a win against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=NOP vs MIN Jan 23, 2021 {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/nop-vs-min-0022000246/box-score#box-score|access-date=2021-01-24|website=www.nba.com}}</ref>

On September 15, 2021, Vanderbilt re-signed with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES RE-SIGN JARRED VANDERBILT AND JORDAN MCLAUGHLIN|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-re-sign-jarred-vanderbilt-and-jordan-mclaughlin|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2021|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> He started 67 games for the Timberwolves during the 2021–22 season, averaging career-highs of 6.9 points, 8.4 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/v/vandeja01.html|access-date=2021-11-30|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 12, 2022, Vanderbilt grabbed 10 rebounds and scored 3 points during Minnesota's 109–104 play-in game victory over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401428071|title=Timberwolves 109–104 Clippers (Apr 12, 2022) Box Score|website=ESPN}}</ref>

=== Utah Jazz (2022–2023) ===
On July 6, 2022, Vanderbilt was traded, alongside [[Malik Beasley]], [[Patrick Beverley]], [[Leandro Bolmaro]], the draft rights to [[Walker Kessler]], four future first-round picks, and a pick swap, to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Rudy Gobert]].<ref name="w650">{{cite web | last=Nardinger| first=Taylor | title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Center Rudy Gobert from Utah Jazz | website=NBA.com | date=2022-07-06 | url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-center-rudy-gobert-from-utah-jazz | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref> Vanderbilt made 52 appearances (including 41 starts) for the Jazz during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], recording averages of 8.3 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 2.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278077/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=August 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2023–present)===
On February 9, 2023, Vanderbilt was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/lakers-timberwolves-jazz-russell-westbrook-trade|title=Lakers trading Russell Westbrook to Jazz in 3-team, 8-player deal|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> He made his Lakers debut two days later, recording 12 points, eight rebounds and four assists in a 109–103 win over the [[2022–23 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2023 |title=RUSSELL SHINES IN RETURN TO LAKERS AFTER TRADE BY T-WOLVES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200853 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Vanderbilt logged 26 appearances (24 starts) down the stretch for the Lakers, averaging 7.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.

On September 18, 2023, Vanderbilt agreed to a four-year, $48 million contract extension with the Lakers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/team/transactions/_/name/lal/season/2023|title=Los Angeles Lakers 2023 Roster Transactions|website=ESPN}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/los-angeles-lakers-announce-significant-roster-move-jarred-vanderbilt-re-signed|title=Los Angeles Lakers Announce Significant Roster Move|first=Ben|last=Stinar|date=September 18, 2023|website=Fastbreak on FanNation}}</ref> The deal was fully guaranteed with a player option in the fourth year.<ref name="auto"/> On December 9, Vanderbilt and the Lakers won the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament|inaugural season]] of the [[NBA In-Season Tournament]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-12-10 |title=Lakers take NBA Cup as AD explodes for 41–20 |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/story/_/id/39080368/lakers-win-nba-cup-lebron-james-earns-season-tournament-mvp |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> beating the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]] 123-109. He logged 16 minutes in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lakers 123-109 Pacers (Dec 9, 2023) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401607495 |access-date=2026-04-02 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Vanderbilt made 29 appearances (six starts) for the Lakers in the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], averaging 5.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 1.2 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278077/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=August 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Vanderbilt made 36 appearances (including two starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], recording averages of 4.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 1.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278077/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=August 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He played in 65 games (including three starts) for the team in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 4.4 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278077/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=August 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> The Lakers would go on to make the Western Conference semifinals against the [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]]. In Game 1 of the series, Vanderbilt suffered a full dislocation of his right pinkie while attempting to block a dunk by [[Chet Holmgren]], an injury which visibly exposed the bone and ultimately required stitches.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jarred Vanderbilt dislocates right pinkie, sources say|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48690222/jarred-vanderbilt-dislocates-right-pinky-finger-sources-say|access-date=August 12, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
He won a gold medal with the 2015 USA U16 National Team at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]]. He scored 19 points in 19 minutes of play at the 2017 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], as Team USA defeated the World Select Team 98–87.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420123751/http://www.usab.com/news-events/live-stats/2017/usa-vs-world-select-team-2017.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 20, 2017|title=LiveStats – USA vs World Select Team – Nike Hoop Summit|access-date=April 8, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref>
